diagnostic_evidence.quote: with $\lambda_i u_i = 0$ and $\mu_i(u_i - C_{k(i)}) = 0$ such that

issues.failure_explanation: With $\lambda_i$ the multiplier of $u_i\ge 0$ and $\mu_i$ that of $u_i\le C_{k(i)}$, stationarity of the minimization Lagrangian gives $G_i - s_i\rho = \lambda_i - \mu_i$, not $\mu_i-\lambda_i$. Applying complementary slackness to the displayed equation yields, e.g., for $\alpha_k=0$: $G_k-\rho=-\lambda_k\le0$, i.e. $\tau_k\ge-\rho$, the reverse of every inequality in Table tab:kkt. The table (and all later use of it) is consistent with the correct sign, so the displayed premise and the derived characterization are mutually inconsistent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\mu_i-\lambda_i$ by $\lambda_i-\mu_i$ in eq:kkt-stationarity (or equivalently redefine the multipliers), so that complementary slackness yields the table as printed.
issues.overall_effect: The stated derivation of Table tab:kkt is invalid as written; the table itself, the MVP rule, and the algorithm are unaffected because they match the correct KKT conditions.
issues.title: Sign error in the stationarity condition contradicts the KKT table derived from it
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol local correction restores the derivation; no downstream result changes.

issues.failure_explanation: By Table tab:kkt, at an optimal point every $i\in\Iup$ satisfies $\tau_i\le-\rho$ and every $j\in\Idown$ satisfies $\tau_j\ge-\rho$, so $\max_{\Iup}\tau_i\le-\rho\le\min_{\Idown}\tau_j$. Equation eq:bias-bounds asserts the reverse chain $\tau_{i^*}\ge-\rho\ge\tau_{j^*}$, which at exact optimality (where $\Delta\le0$) is false unless $\tau_{i^*}=\tau_{j^*}$. Likewise, the shrinking section claims $-\rho\in[\tau_{j^*},\tau_{i^*}]$ 'from' the KKT table at a non-optimal iterate, which the table does not imply (the current iterate's $\tau$ values need not bracket the optimal multiplier).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State $\tau_{i^*}\le-\rho\le\tau_{j^*}$ at ($\varepsilon_{tol}$-)optimality, and present the shrinking interval as a heuristic estimate rather than a KKT consequence.
issues.overall_effect: The stated justification of the midpoint bias fallback and of the shrinking interval is incorrect; the midpoint estimate eq:bias-midpoint itself is unaffected (symmetric in the two endpoints), and shrinking remains a heuristic protected by unshrinking.
issues.title: Bounds on the optimal threshold $-\rho$ stated with reversed inequalities
issues.why_classification: Correcting the inequality direction and the wording is local; the algorithmic choices and all guarantees survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\alpha^*$-variables at zero tend to freeze early (large

issues.failure_explanation: Criteria eq:s1–eq:s4 are exactly symmetric when each variable is measured by its own score: an $\Idown$-only variable ($\alpha_k=C_k$ or $\alpha_k^*=0$) freezes iff its own $\tau$ exceeds $\tau_{i^*}$, and an $\Iup$-only variable freezes iff its own $\tau$ is below $\tau_{j^*}$. The lemma rewrites the $\alpha^*$ criteria in terms of $\tau_k$ using the identity $\tau_{N+k}=\tau_k+2y_k\varepsilon/100$, and then compares thresholds for different variables in different states; the shift $2y_k\varepsilon/100$ is a pure change of variables and carries no information about which variables freeze more readily. In data terms both freezing conditions are the mirror statements $f(\mathbf{x}_k)<y_k(1+\varepsilon/100)$ vs. $f(\mathbf{x}_k)>y_k(1-\varepsilon/100)$ (with $b\approx\tau_{i^*}\approx\tau_{j^*}$). The displayed equivalences eq:s3-rewritten/eq:s4-rewritten are correct, but the stated conclusions ('easier'/'harder' to freeze, 'both effects grow with $y_k$', early freezing of $\alpha^*$ giving faster iterations) are not established; the same rewriting with $2\varepsilon$ would 'prove' an asymmetry for standard SVR.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the asymmetry interpretation: retain eq:s3-rewritten/eq:s4-rewritten only as a change of variables, note that the criteria are symmetric in each variable's own score, and remove the acceleration claims in the abstract, Section 9, and Conclusion.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's substantive claim, the abstract's statement that the shrinking heuristic is 'shown to introduce an asymmetry', the Section 9 'Effect of shrinking' paragraph, and the Conclusion's claim of 'practical convergence acceleration' from this asymmetry are unsupported. The shrinking heuristic and solver correctness are not affected.
issues.title: Claimed shrinking asymmetry between $\alpha$ and $\alpha^*$ is an artifact of the reference variable, not a real effect
issues.why_classification: No dependent formal result fails and the algorithm is unchanged, but the lemma's advertised qualitative content and a headline claim of the paper must be withdrawn rather than merely reworded.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Free variables ($0 < u_i < C_{k(i)}$) are never frozen.

issues.failure_explanation: Shrinking operates on training points $k$, each carrying two dual variables $\alpha_k$ and $\alpha_k^*$, but the counter test refers to a single 'applicable criterion'. When both variables are at bounds (e.g. $\alpha_k=\alpha_k^*=0$) two criteria eq:s1 and eq:s3 apply and it is unspecified whether both must hold; when one variable is free and the other is at a bound meeting its criterion, freezing $k$ removes the free variable from $\Aactive$, contradicting the stated invariant that free variables are never frozen. As written the procedure is not well defined and may exclude a free (possibly KKT-violating) variable until the next reconstruction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify that $k$ is frozen only if both $\alpha_k$ and $\alpha_k^*$ are at bounds and each satisfies its respective criterion among eq:s1–eq:s4 (with counters tracked accordingly).
issues.overall_effect: The shrinking step of Algorithm alg:smo is ambiguous; a natural reading freezes free variables, degrading progress between reconstructions (correctness is preserved only through the unshrinking check).
issues.title: Per-training-point freezing rule is under-specified and can freeze free variables
issues.why_classification: A short clarifying rule resolves the ambiguity; no guarantee or rate is lost since unshrinking already certifies optimality.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: update $\tau$ from~\eqref{eq:reconstruct}, and continue.  Otherwise, the

issues.failure_explanation: In Algorithm alg:smo the reconstruction and full-violation check are placed after the single \For loop over $t$ has terminated. The instruction 'continue outer loop' has no enclosing loop to resume, so when $\Delta^{\mathrm{full}}>\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$ the pseudocode resets $\Aactive$ but then falls through to the bias computation and returns a solution that is not certified optimal; also counters are not reset. The intended control flow (re-enter optimization on the full set until $\Delta^{\mathrm{full}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$ or maxiter) is described in Section 7.3 but not realized by the pseudocode.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Wrap the iteration and reconstruction in an outer repeat loop that exits only when $\Delta^{\mathrm{full}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$ (or the iteration budget is exhausted), resetting counters on unshrink.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm as written does not deliver its stated guarantee of returning an $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$-optimal (certified) solution when shrinking has frozen a violating variable.
issues.title: Unshrinking step refers to a non-existent outer loop
issues.why_classification: A routine restructuring of pseudocode already described in prose restores the guarantee; no mathematical content is lost.

semi-definite, so the formal convergence proof does not extend to this

issues.failure_explanation: $\Omega^*_{k\ell}=K(\mathbf{x}_k,-\mathbf{x}_\ell)$ is a cross-kernel matrix between $\{\mathbf{x}_k\}$ and $\{-\mathbf{x}_\ell\}$, not a Gram matrix, and is not PSD in general: for RBF with $x_1=1,x_2=-1$ in one dimension, $\Omega^*=[[e^{-4\gamma},1],[1,e^{-4\gamma}]]$ has negative determinant. So the stated reason for $\Omega_s\succeq0$ when $a=+1$ is false (the conclusion holds for sign-invariant kernels because $K_s(x,x')=\tfrac14\langle\varphi(x)+\varphi(-x),\varphi(x')+\varphi(-x')\rangle$). By the same identity with a minus sign, $\Omega_s$ for $a=-1$ is also PSD for the RBF (and any $K(-x,-x')=K(x,x')$, $K(-x,x')=K(x,-x')$) kernel, so the claims that $\eta_s<0$ 'is possible' and that the convergence proof 'does not extend' to $a=-1$ are unsupported for the kernels considered.

failure_location.quote: follows from the fact that $\Omega$ and $\Omega^*$ are individually PSD.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the argument with the feature-map identity $K_s(x,x')=\tfrac14\langle\varphi(x)+a\varphi(-x),\varphi(x')+a\varphi(-x')\rangle$ for sign-invariant $K$, concluding $\Omega_s\succeq0$ for both $a=\pm1$ and extending the convergence statement accordingly (or restrict the non-PSD caveat to kernels lacking sign invariance).
issues.overall_effect: The PSD/convergence discussion for m2 rests on an invalid argument and misstates the $a=-1$ regime; the algorithm's fallback is merely unnecessary, so no computed result is wrong.
issues.title: Incorrect PSD reasoning for the symmetric kernel ($\Omega^*$ is not PSD; $a=-1$ case misjudged)
issues.why_classification: A short standard argument fixes the justification and only strengthens the paper's claims; nothing depending on it fails.
